section_summary: This section documents post-World War II Japanese educational reform and related political developments between July and December 1949. It details the administrative and budgetary challenges of decentralizing the school system and implementing the 6-3-3-4 plan, widespread protests against the proposed University Bill, and communist agitation among teachers and students. It also covers the Japanese Government's shutdown of communist-affiliated Korean schools, South Korean diplomatic and legislative reactions, controversies regarding American military school tuition, and the purge of communist teachers.

subfiles.about: Comprehensive memorandum analyzing administrative, financial, and political obstacles facing post-war educational reform in Japan.
subfiles.from: Richard B. Finn, Foreign Service Officer, Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: This memorandum examines the administrative, budgetary, and political difficulties facing educational reform in occupied Japan. It analyzes the decentralization of schooling, the new 6-3-3-4 system, severe funding deficits under the Dodge budget, and fierce resistance to the proposed University Bill. It also highlights widespread student strikes and growing communist agitation among teachers and universities.
subfiles.title: Problems in Japan's Educational Reform
subfiles.to: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Staff study recommending policy prerequisites and security measures regarding subversive Korean schools in Japan.
subfiles.from: Donald R. Nugent, Lt. Col., Civil Information and Education Section, SCAP
subfiles.summary: This staff check sheet analyzes the security and legal issues surrounding communist-dominated Korean schools in Japan. It recommends clarifying Korean resident status and banning North Korean flags before enforcing Japanese educational regulations. Nugent warns that enforcement may provoke leftist riots requiring Eighth Army troop support.
subfiles.title: Enclosure 2 to Despatch 734: Check Sheet on Korean School Situation

subfiles.summary: OIR Report 5087 assesses Japan's campaign against communist schoolteachers, warning that dubious legal grounds, absent procedural safeguards, and broad political bans threaten to revive prewar academic conformity.
